question: Seven hours after undergoing left hip arthroplasty for chronic hip pain, a 67-year-old woman reports a prickling sensation in her left anteromedial thigh and lower leg. Neurologic examination shows left leg strength 3/5 on hip flexion and 2/5 on knee extension. Patellar reflex is decreased on the left. Sensation to pinprick and light touch are decreased on the anteromedial left thigh as well as medial lower leg. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Left hip arthroplasty -> potential nerve injury -> 70% CHAIN: Prickling sensation in left anteromedial thigh and lower leg -> sensory nerve involvement -> 80% CHAIN: Left leg weakness on hip flexion and knee extension -> motor nerve involvement -> 80% CHAIN: Decreased patellar reflex on the left -> nerve compression or injury -> 75% CHAIN: Decreased sensation to pinprick and light touch on left thigh and lower leg -> sensory nerve dysfunction -> 85% CHAIN: Symptoms localized to anteromedial thigh and lower leg -> specific nerve distribution affected -> 90% CHAIN: Given the distribution of symptoms, the most likely underlying cause is opc. Fibular nerve injury -> 70%
analysis: The patient's symptoms are consistent with a femoral nerve injury. The presentation of decreased strength in hip flexion and knee extension, along with decreased sensation in specific areas innervated by the femoral nerve, points towards this nerve being affected.
